trajectory_summary: This call surfaces a customer who already owns 11 panels and has independently run his own cost-benefit math before the rep even asks a real question. The rep never activates the orphaned_flow protocol despite a clear trigger, never probes system size/ownership/performance, and lets the customer's self-supplied 20-year payback conclusion stand unchallenged before closing the call with a passive door-open line. Energy leaked steadily from the first disclosure onward with no rep intervention to redirect.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear from metadata, but the observed transcript is a clean 'no_appointment' — the rep never attempts to set a next step, book an estimate, or even fully qualify the existing system (ownership, panel brand beyond 'not Ion', whether it's functioning). This should not be coded as a soft decline; it's an unworked orphaned-lead call.

observed_outcome.quote: I appreciate it. Thank you very much. Of course. And thank you. Have a good rest of your day.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Call ends with pleasantries and no booked, tentative, or callback next step. The rep offers only a passive open door ('you know where to call') rather than any owned follow-up action.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures a bill range but never turns it into leverage — no reflection of the $100-150 still being paid on top of an existing panel investment, and no connection to the pool/spa load explanation the customer gives moments later. The flip should have landed around 00:55-01:00, tying the ongoing bill plus pool/spa usage into a reason to explore an add-on system.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar,' but the customer volunteers his actual reason (checking on a tax credit, not new-system interest) unprompted. primary_coaching_focus.topic: orphaned_flow not activated on existing-system disclosure
primary_coaching_focus.quote: to making the investment. We already have 11 panels.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the single structural miss that shapes the whole call — the rep treats an existing panel owner like a fresh lead, skipping ownership/company/working-status questions that would properly qualify (or route) this contact. Fixing this one branch point changes how the entire remaining conversation would have gone.

key_moments.quote: to making the investment. We already have 11 panels.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a textbook orphaned_flow trigger — existing solar owner — but the rep does not switch tracks into the orphaned_flow question set (owned vs leased, original company, panel size, system working). Instead the very next line is a generic bill-amount ask lifted from the standard verify flow.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Yeah. And did you get panels of ion? Were those ion panels you got previously?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep asks only the brand question and gets a 'no' — the one orphaned_flow item that fires — but never follows up with who installed it, whether it's owned or financed, or whether it's functioning. This closes off exactly the intel needed to route this lead correctly.

key_moments.quote: the return on investment, you know, to get another five or 10 panels may drive the cost down to zero, but it would take me twenty years to pay for them.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a direct cost/ROI objection stated in the customer's own words — a clean trigger for the bill-as-villain flip (his real expense is the ongoing utility bill plus pool/spa load, not the panel investment). The rep does not attempt any reframe.

key_moments.quote: Okay. But that's because we got a swimming pool and a spa.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a load-increasing asset (pool + spa) that materially changes his usage profile and would justify a bigger or supplemental system. This is the kind of anchor the rep should reflect back as a forward-pulling hook rather than filing silently.
